title: Adrian Carton de Wiart — the unkillable soldier
sources: Wikipedia: Adrian Carton de Wiart (5 May 1880 – 5 June 1963) — British officer of Belgian and Irish descent; served in the Boer War, WWI and WWII; shot in the face, head, stomach, groin, ankle, leg, hip and ear; blinded in his left eye; survived two plane crashes; tunnelled out of a prisoner-of-war camp; ripped off his own injured fingers when a doctor declined to amputate them; wrote of WWI: 'Frankly, I had enjoyed the war.' Left Oxford for the Boer War under a false name, claiming to be 25, and was shot in the stomach and groin. In Somaliland in 1914 he was shot twice in the face, losing his eye and part of his ear. On the Western Front he lost his left hand in 1915, was shot through the skull and ankle at the Somme, the hip at Passchendaele, the leg at Cambrai and the ear at Arras. Victoria Cross for 2–3 July 1916 at La Boisselle, after three other battalion commanders became casualties. In April 1941 his Wellington bomber's engines failed off Libya; knocked unconscious, he came to in the water, swam ashore and was captured by the Italians; made five escape attempts including seven months of tunnelling, once evading capture for eight days aged 61–62 with an eye patch and one empty sleeve, unable to speak Italian. Oxford DNB: 'With his black eyepatch and empty sleeve, Carton de Wiart looked like an elegant pirate.' Died 1963 aged 83.

Photos (public domain, Wikimedia Commons / Imperial War Museum / National Portrait Gallery): Carton de Wiart as a young officer (1904), as a lieutenant-colonel, Sir William Orpen's 1919 portrait, WWII photographs; the Somme and Passchendaele; Vickers Wellington bombers
Archive film (public domain): 'The Battle of the Somme' (British official film, 1916) — illustrative, not Carton de Wiart himself
Music: It's a Long, Long Way to Tipperary (instrumental, 1910s recording) — public domain

post.facebook:
He was shot in the face, the head, the stomach, the ankle, the leg, the hip and the ear. He wrote: "Frankly, I had enjoyed the war."

Adrian Carton de Wiart dropped out of Oxford at 19, lied about his name and age and went to fight in South Africa — shot in the stomach. In 1914, in Somaliland, he was shot twice in the face and lost his left eye. On the Western Front his left hand was shattered in 1915; when the doctor refused to cut off his fingers, he pulled them off himself. At the Somme he was shot through the skull, at Passchendaele through the hip, then the leg, then the ear. In 1916, when three other commanders went down, he took over all their men and held the line — the Victoria Cross.

In the next war, in his sixties, his bomber crashed into the sea off Libya. He swam ashore and was captured by the Italians. He tried to escape five times, once spent seven months digging a tunnel, and stayed free for eight days disguised as a peasant — with one eye, one hand and not a word of Italian.

He died peacefully in Ireland at 83. One historian called him "an elegant pirate".
